conclusion.label: hedged

report:
### Conclusion
Epidemiological studies indicate a weak inverse association between chocolate intake and stroke risk. However, strong evidence from randomized clinical trials directly proving that eating dark chocolate prevents or lowers stroke risk remains unproven.

### Summary of Evidence

1. **Observational Evidence:** Observational studies and meta-analyses of cohort data report that higher or moderate chocolate consumption is associated with up to a 19% reduction in stroke risk (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0021915017300941; https://www.neurology.org/doi/10.1212/WNL.0b013e31826aacfa).

2. **Low Evidence Certainty:** Systematic reviews highlight that although small inverse associations with stroke are observed, the quality and credibility of the available observational evidence are low to very low, leaving significant uncertainty (https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00394-019-01914-9).

3. **Lack of Proven Causality:** No clinical trials evaluating hard cardiovascular endpoints currently prove a direct causal relationship between dark chocolate intake and reduced risk of major cardiovascular events or stroke (https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-023-50351-6).
